findings.finding: User choices are recorded exactly: explicit allowlists, roles, initial behavior and the two immutable account write commands.
Security, no-side-effect denial, real persistence and bilingual documentation have testable acceptance criteria.
findings.resolution: Accepted; include focused fakes at external boundaries and real PostgreSQL integration for persistence.

findings.finding: A catalog duplicated independently from the parser could become stale.
findings.resolution: Revised spec to require one canonical command-definition registry shared by parser, help and catalog.

findings.finding: Shared Chat source badges must not confer moderation/subscriber privileges in the target channel.
findings.resolution: Use only current target-channel event roles and retain the existing wrong-source-channel guard.

findings.finding: Follower lookup adds scope and freshness behavior outside confirmed decisions.

residualRisks: Permission regression during migration/default resolution; guarded by default-policy matrix tests and fail-closed malformed policy handling.
Help output length; bounded single-message responses and explicit compact hint.
revisionSummary: Critique iteration 1 identified command catalog drift risk; iteration 2 specifies a single shared command definition registry. All criteria are measurable and no open blocking question remains.

selfCritique.accuracy: All requirements map to user answers, issue #17, existing product contracts, or official Twitch findings.
selfCritique.completeness: All listed acceptance criteria have corresponding test classes.
selfCritique.consistency: No conflict between explicit OR permissions, VIP gate, streamer identity override, and immutable account commands.
selfCritique.feasibility: Existing stack supports implementation without new dependencies; persistence is validated on PostgreSQL.
selfCritique.alignment: No UX expert or FND-7 work is started in this phase.
